original_value: This paper investigates the use of fundamental solutions for animating detailed linear water surface waves. We first propose an analytical solution for efficiently animating circular ripples in closed form. We then show how to adapt the method of fundamental solutions (MFS) to create ambient waves interacting with complex obstacles. Subsequently, we present a novel wavelet-based discretization which outperforms the state of the art MFS approach for simulating time-varying water surface waves with moving obstacles. Our results feature high-resolution spatial details, interactions with complex boundaries, and large open ocean domains. Our method compares favorably with previous work as well as known analytical solutions. We also present comparisons between our method and real world examples.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines how fundamental solutions can be used to animate detailed linear water surface waves. We first derive a closed-form analytical solution for efficiently animating circular ripples. We then adapt the method of fundamental solutions (MFS) to generate ambient waves that interact with complex obstacles. Next, we introduce a novel wavelet-based discretization that outperforms the current state-of-the-art MFS approach for simulating time-varying water surface waves with moving obstacles. Our results include high-resolution spatial detail, interactions with complex boundaries, and large open-ocean domains. The method compares favorably with prior work and known analytical solutions, and we also provide comparisons with real-world examples.
